newsitem.title: USA: Mich. district files appeal in bond counsel suit.
newsitem.headline: Mich. district files appeal in bond counsel suit.

text.p: A Michigan school district on Tuesday filed an application with the state supreme court to appeal a recent ruling in a lawsuit against its bond counsel, Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone.

Dennis Pollard, attorney for the Pontiac School District, said the application was filed Tuesday afternoon with the state's high court. He said a decision from the court on whether or not it would hear the case could come within six to seven months.

Pollard said the district was appealing all three rulings made by the Michigan Court of Appeals last month. That court had dismissed a conflict of interest claim against Miller Canfield, and ruled that two remaining claims in the lawsuit should be retried.

The appeals court ruling followed an Oakland County Circuit Court jury verdict in 1994 that found Miller Canfield liable of legal malpractice in its work on a 1991 school bond issue, and awarded the district damages. The judge in the jury trial set a damage award of $25.6 million in the case.

The school district filed the lawsuit in connection with a 1991 $54.6 million bond issue. The district charged that Miller Canfield also represented Kemper Securities Inc, the senior manager for the deal, without the district's consent.

The school district also claimed that Miller Canfield had omitted language in the ballot proposal for the bond issue that would have allowed the district, as it had intended, to use bond proceeds to buy land for a bus service and storage facility.
In addition, the lawsuit claimed the law firm misinterpreted to the district's detriment, the Michigan State School Act of 1979 when the firm helped structure the bond issue.

Thomas Linn, a partner at Miller Canfield, was not available to comment on the filing of the appeal. He has said that the firm's outside litigator doubted the state's high court would take up an appeal.
